Degrades fastStable

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Forgetting hyaluronan needs modification for attachment.
  • Mixing G/M blocks in alginate.

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • “Hyal Needs Help”: Hyaluronan requires peptides for cell attach.

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

How crosslink hyaluronan?

Acrylate with ADH/EDC, then thiol-acrylate.

What is matrigel for?

Maintain ESC pluripotency (diluted) or differentiation (undiluted).

Topic 8 – Synthetic Polymer Scaffolds

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

Synthetics offer consistency over naturals, with tunable degradation for TE.
Mind map: Synthetics → Less issues (No allergens/Batch var) → Examples (PLA/PGA/PLGA/PCL/PEOT/PBT) → Degradation (Bulk/Surface) → Apps (Injectable/Long-term).

Must-Know Facts (max 15 bullet points)

  • Less byproducts, variations, immunogenicity than naturals.
  • PLA: Semicrystalline, brittle, hydrophobic, degrades to lactic acid.
  • Copolymerize with PEG for solubility.
  • PGA: Crystalline, tough, degrades to glycolic acid, for sutures.
  • PLGA: Copolymers, biocompatible, acidic products inflame.
  • PCL: Biocompatible, slow bulk erosion (>3 yrs).
  • PEOT/PBT: Elastic, reversible crosslinks, tunable properties.
  • PPEs/PPAs: Surface erosion, milder response.
  • PPF-DA/PEG-DA: Injectable, fill defects, low strength.
  • Categories: Porous solid (bone) vs hydrogels (soft tissues).
  • Solid: Stable, non-dissolve, hydrolyze.
  • Hydrogels: Fill defects, minimally invasive, incorporate cells.

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

NaturalSynthetic
Variable/biocompatibleConsistent/tunable
Immunogenic riskLess inflammation
From sourcesLab-made

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Thinking synthetics non-biodegradable; many are.
  • Forgetting acidic degradation products.

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • “Synthetic Safe”: Less risks than natural.

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

Advantages of synthetics?

No byproducts/variations/immunogenicity.

Describe PCL.

Good biocompatibility, slow bulk erosion for long-term implants.

Topic 9 – 3D Cell Cultures and Applications

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

3D cultures better mimic in vivo via scaffolds, improving cell behavior over 2D.
Mind map: 3D vs 2D → Why (ECM signals/Topography) → Limitations (Diffusion) → Apps (Regen med/Drug discovery/Bioreactors).

Must-Know Facts (max 15 bullet points)

  • 2D artificial; 3D natural with ECM cues.
  • Control morphology/architecture/components.
  • Cells respond in vivo-like.
  • Matrices: Porous, support growth/differentiation.
  • Chemical mod: Adhesion/degradation/GF release.
  • Limited diffusion in 3D; viability drops over time.
  • Apps: Clinical, in vitro, regen med, drug discovery.
  • Bioreactors: Stirring/perfusion for mass transport.
  • Focal adhesions differ 2D vs 3D.
  • 3D for blood vessels/skin/cartilage.

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

2D Cultures3D Cultures
Flat/rigidDynamic ECM
MisrepresentIn vivo-like
SimpleComplex scaffolds

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Assuming 2D sufficient; trap: why 3D better.
  • Forgetting bioreactor need for large tissues.

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • “3D Real Deal”: 3D mimics real tissue better.

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

Why 3D over 2D?

Reproduces complex environments, better cell responses.

Role of bioreactors?

Provide mass transport for cm-scale tissues.

Active Recall Bank

  • What is a polymer? ____
  • Name two polymerization types: ____ and ____
  • Tg stands for: ____
  • Factor favoring crystallinity: ____ structures
  • Hydrogels are ____-swollen networks
  • Natural polymer example: ____
  • Gelatin from: ____ hydrolysis
  • Hyaluronan needs ____ for cell attachment
  • PLA degrades to: ____ acid
  • PGA used for: ____
  • Synthetic advantage over natural: No ____ variations
  • Crosslinks types: Covalent, ____, entanglements
  • Matrigel for: ____ stem cells
  • Fibrin from: ____ + thrombin
  • Alginate crosslinks with: ____ ions
  • Chitosan from: ____ exoskeletons
  • 3D cultures mimic: ____ environments
  • Limitation in 3D: Limited ____
  • Bioreactors provide: ____ transport
  • Focal adhesions differ in: ____ vs ____

15-Minute Mock Exam

  1. Describe two common techniques for fabricating polymeric scaffolds in tissue engineering.

    Examples include electrospinning and solvent casting/particle leaching; these may not suit ceramics due to material differences.

  2. Compare advantages and limitations of natural vs synthetic polymers for scaffolds.

    Natural: Biocompatible, mimic ECM but variable/immunogenic; Synthetic: Consistent, tunable degradation but may cause inflammation from byproducts.

  3. What properties make an ideal scaffold for tissue engineering?

    Porous, biocompatible, biodegradable at controlled rate, mechanically suitable, supports cell attachment/growth.

  4. Explain the role of hydrogels in scaffold-based tissue engineering.

    Hydrogels provide hydrated 3D environments mimicking soft tissues, allowing cell encapsulation and nutrient diffusion.

  5. Which polymer is commonly used for absorbable sutures and why?

    PGA; crystalline, tough, degrades to natural metabolite glycolic acid via hydrolysis.

  6. How does crystallinity affect polymer properties in scaffolds?

    Increases strength and resistance to dissolution; favored by simple linear structures and slow cooling.

  7. Describe the degradation mechanism for PLGA copolymers.

    Hydrolysis of ester bonds in the main chain, releasing acidic products that may induce inflammation.

  8. Why are bioreactors used in 3D tissue engineering?

    To provide convective mass transport (nutrients/oxygen) via stirring/perfusion for larger-scale tissue development.

One-Page Cheat Sheet Summary

CategoryKey Points
Polymers BasicsNatural (DNA/Collagen), Synthetic (PLA/PE); Suited for scaffolds: Versatile, but deform/toxic.
PolymerizationAddition (PE, non-degradable); Step-growth (PLA/PGA, hydrolyze esters).
Structures/StatesCrystalline (Tm), Amorphous (Tg); Semi-crystalline polymers; Tg decreases with long sides.
PropertiesCrystallinity: Simple/linear favors; Thermal: e.g., PGA Tg 35°C Tm 210°C.
Networks/HydrogelsCrosslinks swell; PHEMA common; Balance swelling/retractive forces.
Natural ScaffoldsCollagen (crosslink glutaraldehyde), Gelatin (hydrolysis), Hyaluronan (acrylate), Fibrin (thrombin), Alginate (Ca), Chitosan (GAG-like).
Synthetic ScaffoldsPLA (brittle), PGA (sutures), PCL (slow degrade), Injectables (PPF-DA).
3D CulturesVs 2D: In vivo-like; Limitations: Diffusion; Apps: Regen med, bioreactors for transport.

entry.title: BME 2104 Tissue Engineering – 7
entry.content:
BME 2104 Tissue Engineering – Lecture 7: Scaffold Foundations (III) Final Revision Notes

Lecture Overview

  • 🔴 Top 8 high-yield topics 八大高頻考點 that appear every year:
    1. Scaffold fabrication techniques 支架製備技術 & porosity creation 孔隙形成
    2. Advantages/disadvantages of classic methods 傳統方法優缺點 (solvent casting-PL, gas foaming, freeze-drying, etc.)
    3. Advanced biofabrication 先進生物製造技術 (electrospinning 靜電紡絲, 3D printing, decellularization 脫細胞)
    4. Hydrogels 水凝膠 & cell encapsulation 細胞封裝
    5. Limitations of conventional scaffolds 傳統支架局限性
    6. Bioreactors 生物反應器 & cultivation strategies 培養策略
    7. Host response to implanted scaffolds 宿主對植入支架的反應 (inflammation → fibrosis 炎症 → 纖維化)
    8. Immunoisolation 免疫隔離 & encapsulated cell therapy 封裝細胞療法

Topic 1 – Scaffold Fabrication Principles & Material Selection 支架製備原則與材料選擇

大圖景 (Big Picture)

Scaffold must mimic native ECM 細胞外基質 mechanically and biologically → material choice dictates fabrication method → porosity 孔隙率 & interconnectivity 互連性 are critical for cell migration 細胞遷移/nutrient diffusion 營養擴散.

必須掌握嘅要點 (Must-Know Facts)

  • 🔴 Soft tissues 軟組織 (skin 皮膚, tendon 肌腱, liver 肝臟, vessels 血管) → synthetic/natural polymers 合成/天然聚合物
  • 🔴 Hard tissues 硬組織 (bone 骨) → metals 金屬, ceramics 陶瓷, polymer-containing composites 含聚合物複合材料
  • 🔴 Scaffold must have high porosity 高孔隙率 (>90% ideal 理想>90%), large surface area 大表面積, interconnected pores 互連孔隙
  • 🔴 Pore size 孔徑: 100–500 μm generally optimal for most tissues
  • 🟢 Fabrication technique depends on polymer solubility 聚合物溶解性, Tg/Tm, biocompatibility needs 生物相容性需求
  • 🔴 All methods aim to create 3D porous structure 3D多孔結構 for cell infiltration 細胞浸潤 & vascularisation 血管化

關鍵公式/圖表 (Key Formulas / Diagrams)

對比表 (Comparison Table)

Property 特性Soft Tissue Scaffolds 軟組織支架Hard Tissue Scaffolds 硬組織支架
Main materials 主要材料PLGA, PLLA, collagen 膠原蛋白, alginate 藻酸鹽HA 羥基磷灰石, β-TCP, Ti鈦, composites 複合材料
Mechanical need 機械需求Elastic 彈性, flexible 柔韌High compressive strength 高抗壓強度
Typical fabrication 典型製備Polymer-based (foaming發泡, electrospinning靜電紡絲)Ceramic sintering陶瓷燒結, metal mesh金屬網

常見錯誤同考官陷阱 (Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps)

  • 忘記陶瓷單獨用於軟組織承重時太脆 (Forgetting that ceramics alone are too brittle for load-bearing soft tissue)
  • 以為金屬總係用於軟組織 (Thinking metals are always used for soft tissue) - 實際上唔係

Topic 2 – Conventional Porosity Techniques 傳統造孔技術

大圖景 (Big Picture)

Five classic ways to make pores; each has trade-offs in interconnectivity, solvent use, and pore control.

必須掌握嘅要點 (Must-Know Facts)

  • 🔴 Solvent-casting + particulate leaching (SCPL) 溶劑鑄造+粒子浸出 – gold standard 金標準, uses salt/sugar, highly interconnected
  • 🔴 Gas foaming 氣體發泡 – no organic solvent 無有機溶劑 (advantage), but mostly closed pores 閉孔
  • 🔴 Gas foaming + particulate leaching 氣體發泡+粒子浸出 – solves interconnectivity problem
  • 🔴 Melt molding 熔融成型 – no solvent, uses heat + porogen 致孔劑 (e.g., gelatin particles)
  • 🔴 Phase separation 相分離 – low temperature, good for incorporating growth factors 生長因子
  • 🔴 Freeze-drying 冷凍乾燥 – emulsion or non-emulsion, pore size controlled by freezing rate/pH

關鍵圖表 (Key Diagrams)

對比表 (Comparison Table)

Method 方法Solvent? 使用溶劑?Interconnected pores? 互連孔隙?Pore control 孔徑控制Bioactive molecule friendly? 對生物活性分子友好?
SCPLYesExcellent 優秀Good 良好No (solvent)
Gas foamingNoPoor (closed) 差 (閉孔)Poor 差Yes
Gas foaming + PLNoExcellent 優秀Good 良好Yes
Melt moldingNoGood 良好Good 良好No (high T)
Phase separationYesExcellent 優秀Good 良好Yes (low T)
Freeze-dryingYes/NoExcellent 優秀Excellent 優秀Yes

常見錯誤 (Common Mistakes)

  • 話氣體發泡單獨使用能提供高互連性 (Saying gas foaming alone gives high interconnectivity) - 實際上唔得
  • 忘記聚合物必須不溶於水但致孔劑必須水溶 (Forgetting polymer must be insoluble in water but porogen must be water-soluble)

Topic 3 – Advanced Biofabrication Techniques 先進生物製造技術

大圖景 (Big Picture)

Move from random porosity to precise, reproducible 3D architecture 3D結構 + ability to include cells during printing.

必須掌握嘅要點 (Must-Know Facts)

  • 🔴 Electrospinning 靜電紡絲 → nanofibers 納米纖維, excellent for ECM mimicry, cheap & fast
  • 🔴 Rapid prototyping 快速原型 / 3D printing 3D打印 / microstereolithography 微立體光刻 → CAD-CAM control CAD-CAM控制 of exact geometry
  • 🔴 Microsphere sintering 微球燒結 → trabecular bone-like pores 小梁骨樣孔隙
  • 🔴 Decellularized organs 脫細胞器官 → keep native vascular network 血管網絡 (Ott 2008, 2010 – perfused lung 灌注肺)
  • 🟢 Decellularization + recellularization 脫細胞+再細胞化 = whole organ engineering gold standard 全器官工程金標準

對比表 (Comparison Table)

Technique 技術Resolution 分辨率Speed 速度Cell inclusion during fab? 製造時包含細胞?Vascular network? 血管網絡?
Electrospinning 靜電紡絲Nano 納米Fast 快No 否No 否
3D Bioprinting 3D生物打印50–100 μmSlow 慢Yes (bioink 生物墨水)Possible 可能
Decellularization 脫細胞Native 原生Slow 慢No (recell later 稍後再細胞化)Yes (native 原生)

考官陷阱 (Examiner Trap)

學生忘記脫細胞支架已經擁有完美嘅血管樹 (Students forget decellularized scaffolds already have perfect vascular tree)

Topic 4 – Hydrogels & Cell Encapsulation 水凝膠與細胞封裝

大圖景 (Big Picture)

Hydrogels 水凝膠 = water-swollen polymer networks 水溶脹聚合物網絡; unique ability to encapsulate live cells during gelation.

必須掌握嘅要點 (Must-Know Facts)

  • 🔴 Gelation triggers 凝膠化觸發: chemical crosslinking 化學交聯, UV, temperature, ionic (Ca²⁺ for alginate 藻酸鹽鈣交聯)
  • 🔴 Advantages: cells encapsulated in true 3D, cytocompatible gelation possible 細胞兼容性凝膠化
  • 🔴 GelMA, PEG, alginate most common
  • 🔴 Photoencapsulation 光封裝 allows spatial patterning 空間圖案化
  • 🔴 Major limitation inside thick hydrogels: diffusion limit 擴散限制 → necrosis 壞死 in centre after ~200–300 μm

Topic 5 – Limitations of Conventional Scaffolds 傳統支架嘅局限性

大圖景 (Big Picture)

Traditional methods cannot give precise internal channels or full interconnectivity → poor vascularisation in thick constructs.

必須掌握嘅要點 (Must-Know Facts) (memorise the list)

  • Poor control of pore size/geometry/spatial distribution 孔徑/幾何形狀/空間分佈
  • Lack of predefined internal channels 預定義內部通道
  • Incomplete porogen leaching 不完全嘅致孔劑浸出 in thick scaffolds
  • Closed pores 閉孔 in gas foaming (10–30% interconnected)
  • Residual toxic solvents 殘留有毒溶劑
  • Cell seeding inefficient 細胞接種效率低 (cells stay on surface, <500 μm penetration)

Topic 6 – Bioreactors in Tissue Engineering 組織工程中嘅生物反應器

大圖景 (Big Picture)

Static culture fails → bioreactors provide nutrient flow 營養流 & mechanical signals 機械信號.

必須掌握嘅要點 (Must-Know Facts)

  • 🔴 Purposes: mass transport 物質傳輸, chemical signals 化學信號, mechanical conditioning 機械調節
  • 🔴 Types: spinner flask 旋轉瓶, rotating wall vessel 旋轉壁容器, perfusion cartridges 灌注盒
  • 🔴 Perfusion 灌注 → uniform cell/matrix distribution throughout scaffold
  • 🟢 Mechanical loading 機械負荷 examples:
    • Cyclic compression 週期性壓縮 → ↑ GAG 糖胺聚糖/collagen in cartilage
    • Stretch 拉伸 → aligned collagen & tenascin 腱生蛋白 in ligament

對比表 (Comparison Table)

Culture Method 培養方法Cell distribution 細胞分佈Mass transport 物質傳輸Mechanical signals 機械信號
Static 靜態Surface only 僅表面Diffusion 擴散None 無
Spinner flask 旋轉瓶Better 較好Convection 對流Minimal 極小
Perfusion 灌注Homogeneous 均勻Excellent 優秀Flow/shear 流動/剪切
Rotating vessel 旋轉容器Good 良好Good 良好Low shear 低剪切

Topic 7 – Host Response to Implanted Biomaterials 宿主對植入生物材料嘅反應

大圖景 (Big Picture)

Injury → hemostasis 止血 → inflammation 炎症 → granulation 肉芽組織形成 → foreign body reaction 異物反應 → fibrosis/encapsulation 纖維化/包裹.

必須掌握嘅要點 (Must-Know Facts)

  • 🔴 Sequence: Hemostasis 止血 → Acute inflammation 急性炎症 (neutrophils 中性粒細胞) → Chronic inflammation 慢性炎症 (macrophages 巨噬細胞) → Granulation tissue 肉芽組織 → Foreign body giant cells 異物巨細胞 → Fibrous capsule 纖維囊
  • 🔴 Biomaterials cause non-specific inflammation 非特異性炎症, NOT immune rejection 非免疫排斥
  • 🔴 Final usual outcome = fibrous encapsulation 纖維包裹 (acellular collagen capsule)
  • 🔴 Capsule thicker with: motion 移動, sharp edges 銳邊, leaching monomers 單體浸出, corrosion 腐蝕

Topic 8 – Immunoisolation & Encapsulated Cell Therapy 免疫隔離與封裝細胞療法

大圖景 (Big Picture)

Physical barrier protects allogeneic/xenogeneic cells 同種異體/異種細胞 from immune attack while allowing nutrient/waste/hormone exchange.

必須掌握嘅要點 (Must-Know Facts)

  • 🔴 Classic example: alginate-polylysine microcapsules 藻酸鹽-聚賴氨酸微膠囊 for pancreatic islets 胰島
  • 🔴 Membrane MWCO (Molecular Weight Cut-Off) 分子量截留值 typically 50–150 kDa (lets insulin/glucose through, blocks antibodies)
  • 🔴 Allows use of non-autologous cells 非自體細胞 without immunosuppression 無需免疫抑制

Active Recall Bank 主動回憶庫

  1. Name 3 porosity methods that avoid organic solvents 三種避免使用有機溶劑嘅造孔方法
  2. Which method gives closed pores if used alone? 邊種方法單獨使用會產生閉孔？
  3. What is the main advantage of decellularized organs? 脫細胞器官嘅主要優勢係咩？
  4. Why do cells die in the centre of thick hydrogels? 點解厚水凝膠中心嘅細胞會死亡？
  5. Name the sequence of host response stages (6) 列出宿主反應階段嘅順序（6個）
  6. What cells dominate acute vs chronic inflammation? 急性 vs 慢性炎症中主導嘅細胞係咩？
  7. What is the usual final fate of a non-degradable implant? 不可降解植入物通常嘅最終命運係咩？
  8. Best bioreactor for uniform cell seeding in thick scaffolds? 用於厚支架均勻接種細胞嘅最佳生物反應器？
  9. Two mechanical signals used in bioreactors for cartilage? 用於軟骨嘅生物反應器中嘅兩種機械信號？
  10. Material of choice for soft vs hard tissue scaffolds? 軟組織 vs 硬組織支架嘅材料選擇？
  11. Pore size range generally optimal? 通常最佳嘅孔徑範圍？
  12. Name one natural hydrogel polymer used for encapsulation 一種用於封裝嘅天然水凝膠聚合物
  13. What does “foreign body giant cell” indicate? “異物巨細胞”表明咩？
  14. Why is perfusion better than static culture? 點解灌注培養好過靜態培養？
  15. Example of self-organized vascularised tissue from iPSCs? 來源於iPSC嘅自組織血管化組織例子？
  16. What does SCPL stand for and what porogen is commonly used? SCPL代表咩？常用咩致孔劑？
  17. Which fabrication method is best for incorporating growth factors without denaturation? 邊種製備方法最適合加入生長因子而不使其變性？
  18. What is the main drawback of melt molding? 熔融成型嘅主要缺點係咩？
  19. What does Re < 2000 mean in microfluidics? 微流體中 Re < 2000 代表咩？
  20. Classic encapsulated cell therapy target disease? 經典嘅封裝細胞療法目標疾病？

(Answers at bottom – cover first! 答案在底部 – 先遮住!)

15-Minute Mock Exam 15分鐘模擬考試

  1. Compare advantages and disadvantages of solvent-casting particulate leaching versus gas foaming/particulate leaching combination. (8 marks)

    SCPL 溶劑鑄造粒子浸出: excellent interconnectivity 互連性優秀, good pore control 孔徑控制良好, but uses toxic organic solvent 但使用有毒有機溶劑. Gas foaming + PL 氣體發泡+粒子浸出: no solvent (more biocompatible) 無溶劑 (更生物相容), excellent interconnectivity 互連性優秀, retains temperature-sensitive molecules 保留溫度敏感分子, slightly more complex process 過程稍複雜.

  2. Explain why conventional scaffold techniques fail to produce clinically relevant thick tissues (>1 cm). Give two biological reasons and one fabrication reason. (6 marks)

    Diffusion limitation 擴散限制 of oxygen/nutrients (<200–300 μm), lack of pre-formed vascular channels 預成型血管通道, poor cell penetration 細胞滲透 during seeding (cells remain on surface 細胞停留在表面).

  3. Describe the host response timeline from implantation to fibrous encapsulation. (8 marks)

    Injury 損傷 → hemostasis & platelet activation 止血 & 血小板激活 → acute inflammation 急性炎症 (neutrophils 中性粒細胞) → chronic inflammation 慢性炎症 (macrophages/monocytes 巨噬細胞/單核細胞) → granulation tissue 肉芽組織 + angiogenesis 血管生成 → foreign body giant cells 異物巨細胞 → fibrous capsule formation 纖維囊形成 (weeks–months 數週-數月).

  4. A company wants to implant insulin-producing cells from pig into diabetic patients without immunosuppression. Suggest and justify a tissue-engineering strategy. (6 marks)

    Encapsulate 封裝 porcine islets 豬胰島 in alginate-polylysine microcapsules 藻酸鹽-聚賴氨酸微膠囊 (immunoisolation 免疫隔離). Membrane permits glucose/insulin diffusion 葡萄糖/胰島素擴散 but excludes immune cells/antibodies 免疫細胞/抗體 → prevents rejection 防止排斥 while allowing function.

  5. State four essential requirements of a tissue engineering bioreactor. (4 marks)

    Controlled temperature/pH 受控溫度/pH, efficient mass transfer 質量傳遞, delivery of chemical signals 化學信號, ability to apply mechanical/electrical signals 機械/電信號.

One-Page Cheat Sheet Summary 一頁速查表總結

Category 類別Key Methods / Materials 關鍵方法/材料Pros 優點Cons 缺點Best for 最適用於
Classic porosity 傳統造孔SCPL, Gas foaming+PL, Freeze-dryingHigh interconnectivity 高互連性Solvent (SCPL) or heat 溶劑或高溫General scaffolds 通用支架
Advanced 先進Electrospinning, 3D printing, DecellularizationPrecise geometry 精確幾何, native vessels 原生血管Slow 慢, expensive 貴Vascularised organs 血管化器官
Cell-friendly 細胞友好Hydrogels (PEG, GelMA, alginate)Encapsulation during gelation 凝膠過程中封裝Diffusion limit 擴散限制3D culture 3D培養, islets 胰島
Cultivation 培養Perfusion bioreactors 灌注生物反應器Uniform cell/matrix 均勻細胞/基質Complex setup 設置複雜Thick constructs 厚構建體
Host response endpoint 宿主反應終點Fibrous encapsulation 纖維包裹Isolates implant 隔離植入物Avascular wall 無血管壁, no integration 無整合Most permanent implants 大多數永久植入物
Immunoisolation 免疫隔離Alginate microcapsules 藻酸鹽微膠囊No immunosuppression 無需免疫抑制Fibrosis of capsules over time 膠囊隨時間纖維化Xenogeneic cells 異種細胞

Active Recall Answers 主動回憶答案:

  1. Gas foaming(+PL) 氣體發泡(+粒子浸出), melt molding 熔融成型, freeze-drying 冷凍乾燥
  2. Gas foaming alone 單獨氣體發泡
  3. Native vascular network retained 保留原生血管網絡
  4. Diffusion limitation 擴散限制
  5. Hemostasis 止血–acute 急性–chronic 慢性–granulation 肉芽組織–giant cells 巨細胞–capsule 囊
  6. Neutrophils 中性粒細胞 vs macrophages 巨噬細胞
  7. Fibrous encapsulation 纖維包裹
  8. Perfusion 灌注
  9. Cyclic compression 週期性壓縮, hydrostatic pressure 靜水壓
  10. Polymers 聚合物 vs ceramics/metals 陶瓷/金屬
  11. 100–500 μm
  12. Alginate 藻酸鹽/collagen 膠原蛋白
  13. Persistent material or wear particles 持續存在嘅材料或磨損顆粒
  14. Overcomes diffusion limit & uniform seeding 克服擴散限制 & 均勻接種
  15. Liver buds 肝芽 (Takebe 2013)
  16. Solvent-casting particulate leaching 溶劑鑄造粒子浸出, NaCl/sugar 氯化鈉/糖
  17. Freeze-drying 冷凍乾燥 or phase separation 相分離
  18. High temperature denatures proteins 高溫使蛋白質變性
  19. Laminar flow 層流
  20. Diabetes (pancreatic islets) 糖尿病 (胰島)

English Version Below

Topic 1 – Scaffold Fabrication Principles & Material Selection

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

Scaffold must mimic native ECM mechanically and biologically → material choice dictates fabrication method → porosity & interconnectivity are critical for cell migration/nutrient diffusion.

Must-Know Facts (max 15 bullet points)

  • 🔴 Soft tissues (skin, tendon, liver, vessels) → synthetic/natural polymers
  • 🔴 Hard tissues (bone) → metals, ceramics, polymer-containing composites
  • 🔴 Scaffold must have high porosity (>90% ideal), large surface area, interconnected pores
  • 🔴 Pore size: 100–500 μm generally optimal for most tissues
  • 🟢 Fabrication technique depends on polymer solubility, Tg/Tm, biocompatibility needs
  • 🔴 All methods aim to create 3D porous structure for cell infiltration & vascularisation

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table

PropertySoft Tissue ScaffoldsHard Tissue Scaffolds
Main materialsPLGA, PLLA, collagen, alginateHA, β-TCP, Ti, composites
Mechanical needElastic, flexibleHigh compressive strength
Typical fabricationPolymer-based (foaming, electrospinning)Ceramic sintering, metal mesh

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Forgetting that ceramics alone are too brittle for load-bearing soft tissue
  • Thinking metals are always used for soft tissue (they aren’t)

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

“Soft = Polymer, Hard = Pottery/Metal” (pottery → ceramics)

Topic 2 – Conventional Porosity Techniques

Big Picture

Five classic ways to make pores; each has trade-offs in interconnectivity, solvent use, and pore control.

Must-Know Facts

  • 🔴 Solvent-casting + particulate leaching (SCPL) – gold standard, uses salt/sugar, highly interconnected
  • 🔴 Gas foaming – no organic solvent (advantage), but mostly closed pores
  • 🔴 Gas foaming + particulate leaching – solves interconnectivity problem
  • 🔴 Melt molding – no solvent, uses heat + porogen (e.g., gelatin particles)
  • 🔴 Phase separation – low temperature, good for incorporating growth factors
  • 🔴 Freeze-drying – emulsion or non-emulsion, pore size controlled by freezing rate/pH

Key Diagrams

Comparison Table

MethodSolvent?Interconnected pores?Pore controlBioactive molecule friendly?
SCPLYesExcellentGoodNo (solvent)
Gas foamingNoPoor (closed)PoorYes
Gas foaming + PLNoExcellentGoodYes
Melt moldingNoGoodGoodNo (high T)
Phase separationYesExcellentGoodYes (low T)
Freeze-dryingYes/NoExcellentExcellentYes

Common Mistakes

  • Saying gas foaming alone gives high interconnectivity (it doesn’t)
  • Forgetting polymer must be insoluble in water but porogen must be water-soluble

Topic 3 – Advanced Biofabrication Techniques

Big Picture

Move from random porosity to precise, reproducible 3D architecture + ability to include cells during printing.

Must-Know Facts

  • 🔴 Electrospinning → nanofibers, excellent for ECM mimicry, cheap & fast
  • 🔴 Rapid prototyping / 3D printing / microstereolithography → CAD-CAM control of exact geometry
  • 🔴 Microsphere sintering → trabecular bone-like pores
  • 🔴 Decellularized organs → keep native vascular network (Ott 2008, 2010 – perfused lung)
  • 🟢 Decellularization + recellularization = whole organ engineering gold standard

Comparison Table

TechniqueResolutionSpeedCell inclusion during fab?Vascular network?
ElectrospinningNanoFastNoNo
3D Bioprinting50–100 μmSlowYes (bioink)Possible
DecellularizationNativeSlowNo (recell later)Yes (native)

Examiner Trap

Students forget decellularized scaffolds already have perfect vascular tree

Topic 4 – Hydrogels & Cell Encapsulation

Big Picture

Hydrogels = water-swollen polymer networks; unique ability to encapsulate live cells during gelation.

Must-Know Facts

  • 🔴 Gelation triggers: chemical crosslinking, UV, temperature, ionic (Ca²⁺ for alginate)
  • 🔴 Advantages: cells encapsulated in true 3D, cytocompatible gelation possible
  • 🔴 GelMA, PEG, alginate most common
  • 🔴 Photoencapsulation allows spatial patterning
  • 🔴 Major limitation inside thick hydrogels: diffusion limit → necrosis in centre after ~200–300 μm

Mnemonics

“Hydrogels = Hotel for cells” – cells check in alive during crosslinking

Topic 5 – Limitations of Conventional Scaffolds

Big Picture

Traditional methods cannot give precise internal channels or full interconnectivity → poor vascularisation in thick constructs.

Must-Know Facts (memorise the list)

  • Poor control of pore size/geometry/spatial distribution
  • Lack of predefined internal channels
  • Incomplete porogen leaching in thick scaffolds
  • Closed pores in gas foaming (10–30% interconnected)
  • Residual toxic solvents
  • Cell seeding inefficient (cells stay on surface, <500 μm penetration)

Topic 6 – Bioreactors in Tissue Engineering

Big Picture

Static culture fails → bioreactors provide nutrient flow & mechanical signals.

Must-Know Facts

  • 🔴 Purposes: mass transport, chemical signals, mechanical conditioning
  • 🔴 Types: spinner flask, rotating wall vessel, perfusion cartridges
  • 🔴 Perfusion → uniform cell/matrix distribution throughout scaffold
  • 🟢 Mechanical loading examples:
    • Cyclic compression → ↑ GAG/collagen in cartilage
    • Stretch → aligned collagen & tenascin in ligament

Comparison Table

Culture MethodCell distributionMass transportMechanical signals
StaticSurface onlyDiffusionNone
Spinner flaskBetterConvectionMinimal
PerfusionHomogeneousExcellentFlow/shear
Rotating vesselGoodGoodLow shear

Topic 7 – Host Response to Implanted Biomaterials

Big Picture

Injury → hemostasis → inflammation → granulation → foreign body reaction → fibrosis/encapsulation.

Must-Know Facts

  • 🔴 Sequence: Hemostasis → Acute inflammation (neutrophils) → Chronic inflammation (macrophages) → Granulation tissue → Foreign body giant cells → Fibrous capsule
  • 🔴 Biomaterials cause non-specific inflammation, NOT immune rejection
  • 🔴 Final usual outcome = fibrous encapsulation (acellular collagen capsule)
  • 🔴 Capsule thicker with: motion, sharp edges, leaching monomers, corrosion

Mnemonics

“Hemostasis → Acute → Chronic → Granulation → Giant cells → Capsule” = HAC3G

Topic 8 – Immunoisolation & Encapsulated Cell Therapy

Big Picture

Physical barrier protects allogeneic/xenogeneic cells from immune attack while allowing nutrient/waste/hormone exchange.

Must-Know Facts

  • 🔴 Classic example: alginate-polylysine microcapsules for pancreatic islets
  • 🔴 Membrane MWCO typically 50–150 kDa (lets insulin/glucose through, blocks antibodies)
  • 🔴 Allows use of non-autologous cells without immunosuppression

Active Recall Bank

  1. Name 3 porosity methods that avoid organic solvents
  2. Which method gives closed pores if used alone?
  3. What is the main advantage of decellularized organs?
  4. Why do cells die in the centre of thick hydrogels?
  5. Name the sequence of host response stages (6)
  6. What cells dominate acute vs chronic inflammation?
  7. What is the usual final fate of a non-degradable implant?
  8. Best bioreactor for uniform cell seeding in thick scaffolds?
  9. Two mechanical signals used in bioreactors for cartilage?
  10. Material of choice for soft vs hard tissue scaffolds?
  11. Pore size range generally optimal?
  12. Name one natural hydrogel polymer used for encapsulation
  13. What does “foreign body giant cell” indicate?
  14. Why is perfusion better than static culture?
  15. Example of self-organized vascularised tissue from iPSCs?
  16. What does SCPL stand for and what porogen is commonly used?
  17. Which fabrication method is best for incorporating growth factors without denaturation?
  18. What is the main drawback of melt molding?
  19. What does Re < 2000 mean in microfluidics?
  20. Classic encapsulated cell therapy target disease?

(Answers at bottom – cover first!)

15-Minute Mock Exam

  1. Compare advantages and disadvantages of solvent-casting particulate leaching versus gas foaming/particulate leaching combination. (8 marks)

    SCPL: excellent interconnectivity, good pore control, but uses toxic organic solvent. Gas foaming + PL: no solvent (more biocompatible), excellent interconnectivity, retains temperature-sensitive molecules, slightly more complex process.

  2. Explain why conventional scaffold techniques fail to produce clinically relevant thick tissues (>1 cm). Give two biological reasons and one fabrication reason. (6 marks)

    Diffusion limitation of oxygen/nutrients (<200–300 μm), lack of pre-formed vascular channels, poor cell penetration during seeding (cells remain on surface).

  3. Describe the host response timeline from implantation to fibrous encapsulation. (8 marks)

    Injury → hemostasis & platelet activation → acute inflammation (neutrophils) → chronic inflammation (macrophages/monocytes) → granulation tissue + angiogenesis → foreign body giant cells → fibrous capsule formation (weeks–months).

  4. A company wants to implant insulin-producing cells from pig into diabetic patients without immunosuppression. Suggest and justify a tissue-engineering strategy. (6 marks)

    Encapsulate porcine islets in alginate-polylysine microcapsules (immunoisolation). Membrane permits glucose/insulin diffusion but excludes immune cells/antibodies → prevents rejection while allowing function.

  5. State four essential requirements of a tissue engineering bioreactor. (4 marks)

    Controlled temperature/pH, efficient mass transfer, delivery of chemical signals, ability to apply mechanical/electrical signals.

One-Page Cheat Sheet Summary

CategoryKey Methods / MaterialsProsConsBest for
Classic porositySCPL, Gas foaming+PL, Freeze-dryingHigh interconnectivitySolvent (SCPL) or heatGeneral scaffolds
AdvancedElectrospinning, 3D printing, DecellularizationPrecise geometry, native vesselsSlow, expensiveVascularised organs
Cell-friendlyHydrogels (PEG, GelMA, alginate)Encapsulation during gelationDiffusion limit3D culture, islets
CultivationPerfusion bioreactorsUniform cell/matrixComplex setupThick constructs
Host response endpointFibrous encapsulationIsolates implantAvascular wall, no integrationMost permanent implants
ImmunoisolationAlginate microcapsulesNo immunosuppressionFibrosis of capsules over timeXenogeneic cells

Active Recall Answers: 1. Gas foaming(+PL), melt molding, freeze-drying 2. Gas foaming alone 3. Native vascular network retained 4. Diffusion limitation 5. Hemostasis–acute–chronic–granulation–giant cells–capsule 6. Neutrophils vs macrophages 7. Fibrous encapsulation 8. Perfusion 9. Cyclic compression, hydrostatic pressure 10. Polymers vs ceramics/metals 11. 100–500 μm 12. Alginate/collagen 13. Persistent material or wear particles 14. Overcomes diffusion limit & uniform seeding 15. Liver buds (Takebe 2013) 16. Solvent-casting particulate leaching, NaCl/sugar 17. Freeze-drying or phase separation 18. High temperature denatures proteins 19. Laminar flow 20. Diabetes (pancreatic islets)

entry.title: BME 2104 Tissue Engineering – Overview
entry.content:
BME 2104 Tissue Engineering – Overview

Lecture 1: 基礎概念

  1. TE定義 (Definition) 🔴
    • 用工程同生命科學嘅原理，整啲 生物替代物 (Biological substitutes) 出嚟，去修復、維持或者改善組織功能。
  2. 歷史與里程碑 (History & Milestones) 🔴
    • 1993年：Langer 同 Vacanti 篇經典論文。
  3. 三大工具與策略 (3 Tools & Strategies) 🔴
    • 細胞 (Cells) - 有生命嘅部分。
    • 支架/材料 (Scaffolds/Materials) - 三維結構。
    • 生長信號/因子 (Growth signals/factors) - 控制細胞行為。
  4. 移植類型 (Transplant Types) 🔵
    • 自體 (Autologous) - 用自己嘢，冇排斥，但數量有限。
    • 同種異體 (Allogeneic) - 用第二個人嘅嘢，有排斥風險。
    • 異種 (Xenogeneic) - 用動物嘢，排斥反應好勁。
  5. 技術挑戰 (Technical Challenges) 🟢
    • 血管生成 (Vascularization)、免疫排斥 (Immune rejection)、神經連接 (Innervation)。
  6. 皮膚應用 (Skin Applications) 🔵
    • 分層：表皮 (Epidermis)、真皮 (Dermis)。
    • 產品例子：Apligraf、Dermagraft。
  7. 軟骨應用 (Cartilage Applications) 🔵
    • 軟骨係 冇血管 (Avascular)，好難自己修復。
    • 常用細胞：軟骨細胞 (Chondrocytes)、間充質幹細胞 (Mesenchymal stem cells)。
  8. 先進技術 (Advanced Tech) 🔵
    • 3D生物打印 (3D bioprinting) - 精準控制結構。
    • 器官晶片 (Organ-on-a-Chip) - 用微流體 (Microfluidics) 模仿器官功能。

Lecture 2: 細胞與生物材料

  • Stem Cells 幹細胞 🔴
    • Embryonic stem cells (ESC) 胚胎幹細胞: 乜都能變 (Pluripotent)。
    • Mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) 間充質幹細胞: 可以變骨、軟骨、脂肪 (Multipotent)。
  • Biocompatibility 生物相容性 🟢: 材料唔可以引起毒性 (Toxicity) 或者有害反應 (Adverse reaction)。
  • Bioreactors 生物反應器 🔵: 用嚟大規模培養細胞同組織嘅設備，可以控制環境 (例如pH、氧氣、流體剪切力 Fluid shear stress)。

Lecture 3: 發育生物學

  • Germ Layers 胚層 🔴
    • 外胚層 (Ectoderm): 變表皮、神經系統。
    • 中胚層 (Mesoderm): 變肌肉、骨、血液、血管。
    • 內胚層 (Endoderm): 變肺、肝、腸等內臟。
  • Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) 上皮-間質轉化 🟢: 上皮細胞失去黏附性，變成可以遷移 (Migrate) 嘅間質細胞，對發育同癌症好重要。
  • Extracellular Matrix (ECM) 細胞外基質 🔴
    • 主要成分：膠原蛋白 (Collagen) (提供強度)、蛋白聚糖 (Proteoglycans) (好似海綿，保持水分)。

Lecture 4: 細胞信號與黏附

  1. Fibronectin 纖連蛋白 & RGD Sequence (Arg-Gly-Asp) 🔴: 細胞點樣黐喺ECM上面，主要靠RGD呢個三肽序列。
  2. Focal Adhesions 黏著斑 in 2D vs 3D 🔵: 2D環境下黏著斑大而穩定；3D環境下細而動態，更似真實情況。
  3. Cell Migration 細胞遷移 & Chemotaxis 趨化性 🟢: 細胞跟住化學信號梯度 (Chemical gradient) 移動。
  4. Signal Transduction 信號轉導 🔴: 過程係 配體(Ligand) → 受體(Receptor) → 信號傳遞(Signaling cascade) → 細胞反應(Cellular response)。
  5. G-Protein Coupled Receptors (GPCRs) G蛋白偶聯受體 🟢: 一大類受體，激活後會影響細胞內第二信使 (Second messengers)。
  6. Receptor Tyrosine Kinases (RTKs) 受體酪氨酸激酶 🟢: 另一大類受體，激活後會啟動 MAPK pathway 等重要途徑，影響細胞生長、分化。
  7. Mechanotransduction 機械轉導 🔵: 細胞點樣將 機械力 (Mechanical force) (例如拉扯、壓力) 轉化成 生化信號 (Biochemical signals)。

Lecture 5: 機械生物學與支架

  1. Tensegrity Model 張拉整體模型 🔴: 解釋細胞骨架 (Cytoskeleton) 好似一個張拉結構，將外力傳遍成個細胞。
  2. Integrins 整合素 🔴: 係最主要嘅 機械感受器 (Mechanoreceptors) 同黏附分子，連接細胞內部同外部ECM。
  3. Effect of Mechanical Forces on Differentiation 機械力對分化嘅影響 🔵: 基質硬度 (Matrix stiffness) 可以直接影響幹細胞變成乜嘢細胞 (例如，硬基質傾向變骨細胞)。
  4. Scaffold Requirements 支架要求 🟢:
    • 生物相容性 (Biocompatible)
    • 有適當孔隙 (Porous) 俾細胞生長同營養運輸
    • 降解速度要匹配組織生長速度 (Degradable)
  5. Types of Scaffolds 支架類型 🔴:
    • Bioinert 生物惰性: 唔同身體反應，例如用喺髖關節置換嘅鈦金屬。
    • Bioactive 生物活性: 會同身體互動，促進組織結合，例如羟基磷灰石 (Hydroxyapatite)。
    • Bioresorbable 生物可吸收: 完成任務後會俾身體分解吸收，例如PLGA聚合物。
  6. Scaffold Materials 支架材料 🔵:
    • 天然 (Natural): 膠原蛋白、海藻酸鹽 (Alginate)。優點：生物活性好；缺點：力學性能弱、批次差異大。
    • 合成 (Synthetic): PLA, PGA, PLGA。優點：力學可控、降解可調；缺點：缺乏生物識別位點 (Lack bio-recognition sites)。

Lecture 6: 聚合物科學與3D培養

  • Polymer Basics 聚合物基礎 🔴: 單體 (Monomer) 聚合 (Polymerize) 成 聚合物 (Polymer)。
  • Hydrogels 水凝膠 🔵: 交聯嘅親水聚合物網絡，可以鎖住大量水分。用於 細胞封裝 (Cell encapsulation)。
  • 3D vs 2D Cell Culture 3D與2D細胞培養比較 🔵:
    • 2D: 細胞平鋪生長，行為不自然，但操作簡單。
    • 3D: 細胞在立體環境生長，更似體內情況，細胞信號、機械力、分化都更準確。
  • Natural Polymer Examples 天然聚合物例子 🔴: 膠原蛋白 (Collagen)、纖維蛋白 (Fibrin)、透明質酸 (Hyaluronic acid)。

Lecture 7: 生物製造與臨床挑戰

  1. Classic Scaffold Fabrication 傳統支架製備技術 🔵:
    • Solvent Casting & Particulate Leaching 溶劑澆鑄-粒子浸出: 用鹽粒做孔，溶解後留低孔隙。優點：易控制孔隙率；缺點：用有機溶劑 (Organic solvent)。
    • Gas Foaming 氣體發泡: 用高壓氣體整出氣孔。優點：唔使溶劑；缺點：可能形成閉孔 (Closed pores)。
    • Freeze-Drying 冷凍乾燥: 水溶液結冰後昇華 (Sublimation) 留低孔隙。優點：適合熱敏感材料；缺點：可能結構不均勻。
  2. Advanced Biofabrication 先進生物製造 🔵:
    • Electrospinning 靜電紡絲: 整出納米纖維 (Nanofibers)，模仿天然ECM結構。
    • 3D Bioprinting 3D生物打印: 將細胞同材料一齊精確打印。
    • Decellularization 脫細胞: 將捐贈組織嘅細胞洗走，留低天然嘅ECM支架。
  3. Bioreactors 生物反應器 🔵: 動態培養系統，可以施加 流體剪切力 (Fluid shear stress)、壓縮力 (Compression) 等，促進組織成熟。
  4. Host Response 宿主反應 🟢:
    • 植入後會引發炎症 (Inflammation)。
    • 如果材料生物相容性差或降解產物有刺激，可能會發展成纖維化/疤痕包裹 (Fibrosis/Scar encapsulation)，隔離植入物，導致功能失敗。
  5. Immunoisolation 免疫隔離 🔵:
    • 用半透膜 (Semi-permeable membrane) 包住移植嘅細胞，容許營養同廢物交換，但阻止免疫細胞同抗體進入攻擊細胞。
    • 應用：治療糖尿病嘅 封裝胰島細胞療法 (Encapsulated islet cell therapy)。

entry.title: BME 2104 Tissue Engineering – 1
entry.content:
BME 2104 Tissue Engineering – 1

Exam Overview

  • Exam date & duration: Mid-December 2025 (likely 7-19 Dec), 2-3 hours
  • Top 8 topics that appear every year: Definitions of TE, History & Pioneers, Strategies/Tools, Technical Challenges, Transplant Types, Skin Applications, Cartilage Applications, Advanced Tech (e.g., 3D Printing)
  • Colour code: 🔴 Memorise | 🟢 Understand | 🔵 Apply

BME 2104 組織工程 Tissue Engineering – Final Revision Notes（中英對照版）

Overview

  1. TE定義 Definition
  2. 歷史與里程碑 History & Milestones
  3. 三大工具與策略 3 Tools & Strategies
  4. 移植類型 Transplant Types
  5. 技術挑戰 Technical Challenges
  6. 皮膚應用 Skin Applications
  7. 軟骨應用 Cartilage Applications
  8. 先進技術 Advanced Tech (3D printing, Organ-on-Chip)
  • Colour code 顏色代號: 🔴 要背晒 Memorise | 🟢 要明 Understand | 🔵 要識用 Apply

Topic 1 – Course Structure & Assessments 課程結構與評核

Big Picture 總覽

整個課程圍繞「點樣用細胞+支架+訊號」去解決器官短缺問題。

Topic 2 – Motivation 點解要讀組織工程？

Big Picture

因為好多器官唔會自己生返，捐贈又少，人等緊等緊就死晒。
Mind map: 疾病 → 無再生能力 → 器官短缺 → TE救命

Must-Know Facts

  • 🔴 香港器官捐贈率全球最低，等器官平均5年，最長29年
  • 🔴 每年需求: Skin 300萬、Bone/Cartilage/Blood vessel 各100萬、Kidney 60萬
  • 🟢 Christopher Reeve 超人演員 → 脊椎受傷終身癱瘓 → 代表性案例
  • 🔵 目標: Repair 修補 | Restore 恢復 | Regenerate 再生 | Replace 取代

Mnemonics

  • 香港三個關鍵字: 「最低、最多、最長」→ 捐贈率最低、等緊人最多、等最長

Topic 3 – History 歷史

Must-Know Timeline（背晒）

  • 1000 BC 古印度鼻移植
  • 16世紀 Tagliacozzi 用手臂皮瓣整鼻
  • 1962 首個合成皮膚
  • 1985 Langer & Vacanti 正式提出「Tissue Engineering」
  • 1996 Dolly 多利羊（第一隻複製哺乳動物）
  • 1997 Vacanti Mouse 老鼠背長人耳（PLGA + 軟骨細胞）

Mnemonics

  • 「96羊97鼠」→ Dolly 96年，Vacanti Mouse 97年

Topic 4 – Definitions 定義（必背金句）

Langer & Vacanti (1993) 最經典

「Tissue engineering is an interdisciplinary field that applies the principles of engineering and life sciences toward the development of biological substitutes that restore, maintain, or improve tissue or organ function.」
組織工程係一個跨學科領域，用工程同生命科學嘅原理，去開發可以恢復、維持或改善組織或器官功能嘅生物替代品。

三大工具 Three Tools（CSS）

  • Cells 細胞 → 活嘅部分
  • Scaffolds 支架 → 結構支撐（要可降解）
  • Signals 訊號 → 生長因子或機械刺激

TE vs Regenerative Medicine 對比

TE 組織工程Regenerative Medicine 再生醫學
In vitro 體外培養In vivo 體內直接刺激
嚴格控制環境用身體自己嘅調節

Topic 5 – Transplant Types 移植類型

四大類（背晒優缺點）

類型來源優點缺點
Autograft自己無排斥痛、來源少
Allograft其他人來源較多排斥、捐贈者少
Xenograft動物來源多排斥+感染風險
Man-made人工心/肺即用機械故障

Mnemonics

  • 「自家無痛、他人排斥、動物染病」→ Auto無排斥、Allo排斥、Xeno感染

Topic 6 – Technical Challenges 技術挑戰

四大死穴（考試最愛問）

  1. Vascularization 血管化 → 細胞離毛細血管要<100μm
  2. Scale-up 放大 → 點樣做出有臨床意義嘅大小
  3. Microenvironment 微環境 → 營養、訊號、力學
  4. Cell source & control 細胞來源同控制分化/增生

Mnemonics

  • 「血管、放大、微環境、細胞」→ 血大微細

Topic 7 – Successful Applications 成功案例

Skin 皮膚（最成熟）

  • Epicel → 自体角質細胞薄片（超薄，易碎）
  • Apligraf → 同種異體（纖維母細胞+角質細胞），3星期培養，有真皮層

Cartilage 軟骨

  • Carticel → 自体軟骨細胞注射
  • Hyalograft-C → 細胞+支架，效果更好

Bladder 膀胱（Atala 2006）

  • 首個成功移植實驗室培養嘅器官（用自体細胞+可降解支架）

Topic 8 – Advanced & Future 未來技術

  • 3D Bioprinting 生物3D打印
  • Organ-on-a-Chip 器官晶片（藥物測試，減少動物試驗）
  • Decellularized ECM 去細胞基質（Badylak）
  • Microfluidic vascular networks 微流控血管網

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

  1. 香港等器官平均幾耐？ _____ → 5年（最長29年）
  2. Vacanti Mouse 用咩物料？ _____ → PLGA
  3. TE三大工具？ _____ → Cells, Scaffolds, Signals
  4. Autograft 最大缺點？ _____ → 痛、來源少
  5. 皮膚產品 Apligraf 用咩細胞？ _____ → 同種異體纖維母細胞+角質細胞
  6. 細胞點樣先有營養？ _____ → <100μm 離毛細血管
  7. 首個移植實驗室膀胱嘅人係邊個？ _____ → Anthony Atala

English Version Below

Topic 1 – Motivation for Tissue Engineering

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

Tissue engineering addresses the critical shortage of organs and tissues for transplantation by creating viable substitutes.
Mind map: Need → Diseases (SCI/Parkinson’s/Alzheimer’s/Heart) → Shortage (Waitlists/Deaths) → Limited Regeneration → TE Solutions

Must-Know Facts (max 12 bullet points)

  • 🔴 Millions suffer from damaged tissues (e.g., Spinal Cord Injury, Parkinson’s)
  • 🟢 Most tissues don’t regenerate spontaneously after damage
  • 🔴 HK organ shortage: Lowest donation rates, >3,000 waiting, avg 5-29 years
  • 🟢 Waitlist: 1 added every 10 min; only 80 transplants/day
  • 🔴 Annual needs: Skin 3M, Bone/Cartilage/Vessel 1M each, Kidney 600K, Liver/Nerve 200K
  • 🟢 Examples: Christopher Reeve (SCI from accident)
  • 🔵 Congenital abnormalities, injuries, diseases drive need
  • 🟢 TE aims: Repair/Restore/Regenerate/Replace

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

Regenerating vs Non-Regenerating TissuesYes (Regenerate)No (Don’t)
ExamplesBone, EpidermisCardiac Muscle, Nerve
ReasonsStem cells presentLimited vasculature/proliferation
ImplicationsSelf-heal small defectsNeed TE/transplants

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Assuming all muscles regenerate (skeletal/cardiac don’t fully)
  • Forgetting stats like annual procedures – trap: vague answers without numbers
  • Mixing HK-specific shortage with global waitlists

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • Needs: “Skinny Bones Never Bleed Lots, Can’t Keep Bladder Strong” – Skin, Bone, Nerve, Blood vessel, Liver, Cartilage, Kidney, Bladder, Skeletal Muscle
  • Waitlist: “10 min add, 80 day transplants” – 10-80 rule

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

Why is there a need for tissue engineering? Give examples.

Due to limited regeneration and organ shortages causing deaths; e.g., Spinal Cord Injury (no repair), HK waits up to 29 years for organs.

What tissues regenerate spontaneously?

Bone, epithelia (e.g., epidermis); not cardiac muscle or nerves.

Topic 2 – History of Tissue Engineering

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

Tissue engineering evolved from ancient transplants to modern cell-based therapies, driven by medical needs.
Mind map: Ancient (1000 BC nose) → 16-19th C (Skin/Tooth) → 20th C (Transplants/Synthetics) → 1980s (TE Concept) → Milestones (Dolly/Vacanti)

Must-Know Facts (max 12 bullet points)

  • 🔴 Ancient: 1000 BC Sushrutha nose transplants
  • 🟢 16th C: Tagliacozzi forearm flap for nose
  • 🔴 17-18th C: Tooth/Skin/Corneal transplants
  • 🟢 19th C: Sterile technique/anesthesia enable surgery
  • 🔴 20th C: Kidney/Heart/Lung/Bone marrow post-1950
  • 🟢 1962: First synthetic skin
  • 🔴 1985: TE articulated; 1988 first symposium
  • 🟢 Dolly (1996): First cloned mammal, sparks reproduction ideas
  • 🔵 Vacanti Mouse (1997): PLGA scaffold with chondrocytes
  • 🟢 Pet cloning available; human cloning ethical issues
  • 🔵 Shift to cell-based therapies late 20th C

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

Ancient vs Modern TEAncientModern
MethodsAutografts (nose/skin)Scaffolds/Cloning/3D Printing
FocusReconstructionRegeneration/Organ substitutes
TechManual surgeryCells/Biomaterials/Signaling

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Confusing Dolly as human cloning (sheep, 1996)
  • Forgetting ethical concerns in human cloning – trap: ethical Qs
  • Misattributing Vacanti Mouse to human application

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • History: “Nose To Tooth, Skin Cornea, Sterile Transplants” – N(1000BC), T(17C), S/C(18C), S(19C), T(20C)
  • Milestones: “Dolly Vacanti” – D(Cloning), V(Scaffold)

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

Outline the history of tissue engineering from ancient to modern times.

Ancient: 1000 BC nose; 16-19th C skin/tooth; 20th C transplants; 1962 synthetic skin; 1985 TE concept; 1997 Vacanti Mouse.

What was the Vacanti Mouse and its significance?

Mouse with human ear-shaped cartilage grown on back using PLGA scaffold and chondrocytes; popularized TE.

Topic 3 – Definitions and Paradigms

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

Tissue engineering applies biology and engineering to create substitutes that restore tissue function.
Mind map: Definitions → Langer/Vacanti (1993) → Goals (Restore/Maintain/Improve) → Paradigm (Cells/Materials/Factors)

Must-Know Facts (max 12 bullet points)

  • 🔴 Definition (Langer/Vacanti): Biological substitutes to restore/maintain/improve function
  • 🟢 Fung: Understanding structure-function in tissues
  • 🔴 Laurencin: Repair using biomaterials/cells/factors
  • 🟢 Includes cells/tissues/organs/blood
  • 🔵 Paradigm: Cells + Biocompatible materials + Biochemical/Biophysical factors
  • 🟢 TE vs Regenerative Med: In vitro (TE) vs In vivo (RM)
  • 🔴 In vitro advantages: Evaluation/control; disadvantages: Remodeling needed
  • 🟢 In vivo: Physiologic environment; disadvantages: Mechanical stresses

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

TE vs Regenerative MedicineTissue EngineeringRegenerative Medicine
EnvironmentIn vitroIn vivo
AdvantagesControl/evaluationPhysiologic regulators
DisadvantagesNeeds remodelingDislodgement/stresses

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Quoting only one definition – trap: Compare multiple
  • Confusing TE as only for tissues (includes organs/cells)
  • Ignoring biophysical factors in paradigm

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • Definitions: “Langer Vacanti Fung Laurencin” – LVFL (Love Very Fine Laundry)
  • Paradigm: “Cells Scaffold Signals” – CSS (Cascading Style Sheets for tissues)

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

Define tissue engineering according to Langer and Vacanti.

An interdisciplinary field that applies engineering and life sciences to develop biological substitutes that restore, maintain, or improve tissue function.

Compare TE and regenerative medicine.

TE: In vitro, controlled but needs integration; RM: In vivo, natural but prone to stresses.

Topic 4 – Strategies and Tools

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

TE strategies combine cells, scaffolds, and signaling to engineer functional tissues.
Mind map: Tools → Cells (Function/Repair) → Scaffolds (Support/Degrade) → Signaling (Proteins/Mechanical) → Strategies (Isolated Cells/Growth Factors/Cell-Matrix)

Must-Know Facts (max 12 bullet points)

  • 🔴 3 Tools: Cells (living/protein-producing), Scaffolds (structural/biodegradable), Signaling (proteins/mechanical)
  • 🟢 Strategies: Isolated cells/substitutes, Tissue growth factors, Cell-matrix with scaffolds
  • 🔵 Paradigm considerations: Cells, Materials, Biochemical factors (growth), Biophysical (loading)
  • 🟢 Isolated cells: Infusion without surgery
  • 🔴 Growth factors: Targeted delivery/gene systems
  • 🟢 Scaffolds: Grow/replace biodegradable matrix

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

Isolated Cells vs Cell-MatrixIsolated CellsCell-Matrix
MethodInfusionScaffold growth
AdvantagesNo surgeryReplace matrix
ApplicationsSpecific cellsComplex tissues

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Forgetting biophysical factors (e.g., mechanical loading)
  • Assuming scaffolds are permanent – trap: Must be biodegradable
  • Mixing tools with strategies

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • Tools: “Cells Scaffold Signals” – CSS
  • Strategies: “I Grow Cells” – Isolated, Growth factors, Cell-matrix

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

What are the three main tools in TE?

Cells (building blocks), Scaffolds (support), Cell Signaling (direct function).

Describe TE strategies.

Isolated cells for infusion, growth factors for delivery, cell-matrix for scaffold replacement.

Topic 5 – Types of Transplants

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

Transplants vary by source, each with benefits and drawbacks in compatibility and availability.
Mind map: Types → Autograft (Self) → Allograft (Same species) → Xenograft (Other species) → Man-made (Artificial)

Must-Know Facts (max 12 bullet points)

  • 🔴 Autograft: From self; painful, limited source
  • 🟢 Allograft: From another human; donor scarcity, rejection
  • 🔴 Xenograft: From animals; biocompatibility issues, infection risk
  • 🟢 Man-made: Artificial hearts/lungs; no rejection but mechanical failures
  • 🔵 Drawbacks: Autograft (pain/failure in elderly), Allograft (immune), Xenograft (contamination)
  • 🟢 Examples: Skin grafts, organ transplants

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

Autograft vs Allograft vs XenograftAutograftAllograftXenograft
SourceSelfSame speciesOther species
Rejection RiskLowHighHigh
AvailabilityLimitedScarceAbundant
DrawbacksPainfulImmuneInfection

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Claiming autografts have rejection (they don’t)
  • Forgetting man-made as a type – trap: Include in answers
  • Overstating xenograft safety

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • Types: “Auto All Xeno Man” – AAXM (Axe ‘em)
  • Drawbacks: “Pain Scarcity Infection” – PSI (Pressure)

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

Compare types of transplants.

Autograft: Self, no rejection but painful; Allograft: Human, rejection; Xenograft: Animal, infection.

What are drawbacks of xenografts?

Biocompatibility, immune rejection, higher contamination risk.

Topic 6 – Technical Challenges

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

TE faces hurdles in cell biology, materials, microenvironment, and scale-up for clinical use.
Mind map: Challenges → Cell (Differentiation/Proliferation) → Materials (Porosity/Degradation) → Microenv (Signals/Nutrients) → Scale (Vascularization/Automation)

Must-Know Facts (max 12 bullet points)

  • 🔴 Cell Biology: Control diff/prolif, adhesion, immune, environment
  • 🟢 Materials: 3D scaffolds, porosity vs strength, degradation, interactions
  • 🔴 Microenvironment: Reconstitute for function (cells/ECM/signals)
  • 🟢 Scale-up: Enough microenvs, microcirculation (capillaries <100um)
  • 🔵 Automation for clinical scale
  • 🟢 Cell communication/migration
  • 🔴 Post-implant: Slow vascularization, nutrient lack
  • 🟢 Vascular need: Cells near capillaries

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

Cell Biology vs Materials ChallengesCell BiologyMaterials
Key IssuesDiff/Prolif/ImmunePorosity/Degradation
SolutionsSignaling/EnvironmentPolymers/Processing
ImpactFunction/PhenotypeStrength/Support

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Ignoring microenvironment dynamics
  • Underestimating vascularization – trap: Why thick tissues fail
  • Forgetting automation for scale

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • Challenges: “Cells Make Micro Scale” – CMMS (Comms)
  • Microcirculation: “<100um from capillary” – 100 rule

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

What are key technical challenges in TE?

Cell control (diff/prolif), materials (porosity/degrade), microenvironment (signals), scale-up (vascular/automation).

Why is vascularization a challenge?

Cells need nutrients <100um from capillaries; slow ingrowth post-implant.

Topic 7 – Specific Tissue Applications

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

TE has succeeded in avascular tissues like skin, cartilage, bladder, but struggles with complex organs.
Mind map: Apps → Skin (Epicel/Apligraf) → Cartilage (Microfracture/Carticel) → Bladder (Autologous cells/scaffold) → Others (Kidney/Liver challenges)

Must-Know Facts (max 12 bullet points)

  • 🔴 Skin: Epicel (autologous keratinocytes), Apligraf (dermal/epidermal)
  • 🟢 Skin repair: Epithelial regen, Dermal matrix (Alloderm), Full-thickness
  • 🔴 Limitations: Slow vasc, no glands/follicles
  • 🟢 Cartilage: Limited regen; Microfracture, Osteochondral transplants
  • 🔴 Cell-based: Carticel (autologous chondrocytes)
  • 🟢 Scaffold: Hyalograft-C; better in young/athletes
  • 🔴 Bladder: Autologous cells on scaffold; integrated over years
  • 🟢 Success: Avascular tissues; hurdles for vascular (kidney/liver)
  • 🔵 Kidney: Glomerular structure hard
  • 🟢 Liver: Hepatic lobules challenging

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

Skin vs Cartilage TESkinCartilage
MethodsGrafts/Epicel/ApligrafMicrofracture/Carticel/Scaffolds
ChallengesVasc/No glandsLimited sources/Rediff
SuccessCommercializedLong-term in young

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Assuming bladder TE works for all organs (only avascular)
  • Forgetting stem cells in cartilage – trap: Coculture benefits
  • Mixing products (Epicel xenogeneic)

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • Skin Products: “Epic Apple” – Epicel, Apligraf
  • Cartilage: “Micro Osteo Cell Scaff” – MOCS (Mocks)

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

Describe skin TE products.

Epicel: Autologous keratinocytes sheets; Apligraf: Allogeneic dermal/epidermal, air-liquid differentiation.

What are cartilage repair methods?

Microfracture (marrow clot), Osteochondral (harvest plugs), Cell-based (Carticel injection).

Topic 8 – Advanced Technologies and Potential

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

Emerging tech like nanotech, microfluidics, and 3D printing enhance TE for complex organs and testing.
Mind map: Tech → Nanotech/Microfluidics (Scaffolds/Networks) → 3D Printing (Organs/Chips) → Potential (Drug Testing/Heart Membranes)

Must-Know Facts (max 12 bullet points)

  • 🔴 Nanotech: Complex 3D scaffolds mimicking in vivo
  • 🟢 Microfluidics: Vascular networks, <10um resolution
  • 🔴 Solve nutrient transport for organs like liver/kidney
  • 🟢 Organ-on-Chip: Reduce animal testing, vaccine trials
  • 🔴 3D Printing: Heart membranes, blood vessels (sugar)
  • 🟢 Bioengineering: Decellularized matrices
  • 🔵 Drug delivery/high-throughput screening

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

Traditional vs Advanced TETraditionalAdvanced
MethodsScaffolds/CellsNanotech/3D Print/Microfluidics
BenefitsBasic repairVascular/Scale-up
ExamplesVacanti MouseOrgan-on-Chip

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Overhyping 3D printing for full organs (still potential)
  • Forgetting microfluidics for vascular – trap: Nutrient issues

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • Tech: “Nano Micro 3D” – NM3 (Enemy)
  • Potential: “Chip Print Decell” – CPD (Copied)

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

How do microfluidics aid TE?

Create vascular networks for nutrient transport in scaffolds for complex organs.

What is organ-on-a-chip?

3D printed tissues for drug testing, reducing animal use.

Topic 10 – Pioneers and Business

Big Picture (1 sentence + mind map in text)

Pioneers advanced TE from concepts to clinical, with businesses commercializing products.
Mind map: Pioneers → Atala (Organs) → Langer (Systems) → Macchiarini (Trachea) → Others (Badylak/Hamilton) → Business (Organovo/Tengion)

Must-Know Facts (max 12 bullet points)

  • 🔴 Atala (WFIRM): First lab-grown organ transplant (2006)
  • 🟢 Langer (MIT): TE/Controlled release (1993)
  • 🔴 Macchiarini: First donor trachea (2008)
  • 🟢 Khademhosseini: Living tissues/organs in lab
  • 🔴 Badylak: ECM for regrowth
  • 🟢 Hamilton: Organ-on-chip (2011)
  • 🔴 Bhatia: Microchip livers
  • 🟢 Stevens: Biomaterials/regeneration
  • 🔵 Miller: 3D print vessels
  • 🟢 Shah: 3D inks/scaffolds
  • 🔴 Business: Organovo (Bioprinting), Tengion (Neo-Organs)

Key Formulas / Diagrams (use code blocks)

Comparison Table (“X vs Y” in proper Markdown table)

Academic Pioneers vs BusinessPioneersBusiness
FocusResearch/InnovationCommercialization
ExamplesAtala/LangerOrganovo/Tengion
ImpactConcepts/TransplantsProducts/Testing

Common Mistakes & Examiner Traps

  • Misattributing milestones (e.g., Atala first organ)
  • Forgetting business aspects – trap: Commercial viability Qs

Mnemonics / Memory Hooks

  • Pioneers: “Atala Langer Mac Khad Bad Ham Bhat Ste Mil Sha” – ALMKBHBSMS (All Make Big History)
  • Business: “Org Ten” – Organovo, Tengion

Past Exam Questions + Model Answers (use > blockquote for answers)

Who are key TE pioneers?

Atala (first organ), Langer (definitions), Macchiarini (trachea).

Describe a TE business.

Organovo: 3D bioprinting for tissues, collaborates with NIH for drug efficacy.

Active Recall Bank

  • Christopher Reeve suffered from? _____
  • HK organ wait average? _____
  • Dolly was cloned in? _____
  • Vacanti Mouse material? _____
  • TE definition by Langer? _____
  • 3 TE tools? _____
  • Autograft drawback? _____
  • Cell biology challenge? _____
  • Skin product Epicel? _____
  • Cartilage method Microfracture? _____
  • Microfluidics resolution? _____
  • Pioneer Atala milestone? _____
  • Business Organovo focus? _____
  • Paradigm factors? _____
  • Regenerating tissue example? _____
  • History 1985? _____
  • Challenges scale-up? _____

15-Minute Mock Exam

  1. Define tissue engineering and explain its paradigm.

    Interdisciplinary field developing substitutes to restore function; involves cells, materials, biochemical/biophysical factors.

  2. Compare autograft and xenograft.

    Autograft: Self-source, no rejection but painful/limited; Xenograft: Animal, abundant but infection/rejection risk.

  3. What are challenges in cartilage TE?

    Limited regeneration, inefficient redifferentiation, scaling thickness, cell sources.

  4. Describe Apligraf for skin repair.

    Allogeneic fibroblasts in collagen + keratinocytes; 3 weeks, promotes healing despite rejection.

  5. Why vascularization is key challenge?

    Nutrient lack post-implant; cells need <100um from capillaries.

  6. Name a pioneer and contribution.

    Langer: TE concepts and controlled release systems.

One-Page Cheat Sheet Summary

SectionKey Points
AssessmentsExam 50%, Project 20%, Labs/Assign 15% each; Presentations 15 min
MotivationDiseases/shortage; Stats: Skin 3M/yr, Waitlist 10 min add
HistoryAncient nose → 1962 skin → 1997 Vacanti → Dolly cloning
DefinitionsRestore function via cells/scaffolds/signals; TE in vitro vs RM in vivo
StrategiesIsolated cells, Growth factors, Cell-matrix
TransplantsAuto (self), Allo (human), Xeno (animal); Drawbacks: Pain/rejection/infection
ChallengesCell control, Materials porosity, Microenv, Scale vascular
AppsSkin: Epicel/Apligraf; Cartilage: Carticel; Bladder: Scaffold
AdvancedMicrofluidics vascular, 3D print organs, Chip testing
PioneersAtala organ, Langer defs, Organovo bioprint
